purpose: Recheck the rights gate on the 2015 Pansipit juvenile-fish diet study and assess an alternative species-interaction index without treating indexed records as automatically reusable.

accessCheck.indexedText: Publisher search index exposes article scope and selected text; no full PDF bytes or diet table were obtained for this review.

primaryDietSource.scopeRetained: 2012 juvenile-fish gut-content study in the upstream Pansipit River-Lake Taal connection; 12 source-reported species; historical and reach/life-stage limited.

rightsHolderPolicy.source: UPLB University Knowledge Digital Repository JESAM policies
rightsHolderPolicy.finding: Policy says authors assign article copyright to UKDR subject to stated personal-use exceptions; distribution/use of article material outside the exemption requires a written UKDR agreement and attribution.
rightsHolderPolicy.articleCopyrightMetadata: Ateneo metadata reports Publisher Copyright © 2015, University of the Philippines Los Baños, all rights reserved.

primaryDietSource.decision: Keep species-by-food-item table, percentages, and app-facing diet claims unextracted pending written permission or a verified applicable reuse license.

alternativeSourceCheck.sourcePolicy: GloBI describes itself as an open interaction-data service and asks users to cite the original data contributors/datasets; it recommends versioned stable data for research and describes the live API as exploratory. Each underlying dataset still needs source-specific provenance and reuse review.

alternativeSourceCheck.interpretation: A 403 is an access limitation of this query environment, not evidence that the taxa have no recorded prey. No GloBI prey record or license has been admitted for Bangwit.

nextActions: Request written permission from the journal/UKDR or rights holder for the minimal Pansipit species-by-food-item facts and attribution terms; do not send without Joseph review/authorization.
For any GloBI candidate interaction, locate and review its original dataset citation and license, species/rank mapping, prey/predator direction, life stage, and geography before use.
Prefer stable, versioned data publications over live API results for any eventual research projection; retain source IDs, versions, and citations.
If no compatible diet permission or clearly licensed original dataset is found, leave diet as unavailable for those taxa rather than infer prey from broad family descriptions.
